title: 3934. Smallest Unique Subarray

examples.explanation: Subarrays of length 1: [3] → appears 3 times Subarrays of length 2: [3, 3] → appears 2 times Subarrays of length 3: [3, 3, 3] → appears once The subarray [3, 3, 3] is unique, so the smallest unique subarray length is 3.
Subarrays of length 1: [2] → appears 2 times [1] → appears once [3] → appears 2 times The subarray [1] is unique, so the smallest unique subarray length is 1.

Subarrays of length 1: [1] → appears 3 times [2] → appears 2 times Subarrays of length 2: [1, 1] → appears once [1, 2] → appears once [2, 2] → appears once [2, 1] → appears once There is at least one subarray of length 2 that is unique, so the smallest unique subarray length is 2.

hints: Think in terms of checking a fixed length len: count all subarrays of length len, and see whether any one appears exactly once.
Use rolling hash so each subarray can be represented in O(1) after preprocessing, instead of comparing arrays directly.
The answer can be binary searched because if there is a unique subarray of length len, then there is also a unique subarray of some length > len.
For each checked length, store frequencies of hashes in a hashmap. If any hash has frequency 1, that length works.
